## Setup

We use base R for most of the analysis, `MASS` for backward stepwise selection (`stepAIC`),
`ggplot2` for the figures that go in the paper, and `knitr` for the table.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

## Data cleaning

These are the same cleaning steps from Project Update 4, plus two new ones:
(1) we drop athletes with fewer than 5 professional bouts, and (2) we group the
weight classes into four division groups.

```{r}
# read in the data (change the file name here if yours is saved differently)
ufc <- read.csv("ufc_athletes.csv")
nrow(ufc)   # 3,145 athletes

# heights and weights of zero are impossible, so treat them as missing
ufc$height[!is.na(ufc$height) & ufc$height <= 0] <- NA
ufc$weight[!is.na(ufc$weight) & ufc$weight <= 0] <- NA

# total professional bouts and the response variable (career win percentage, 0-100)
ufc$total_fights <- ufc$wins + ufc$losses + ufc$draws
ufc <- subset(ufc, total_fights > 0 & !is.na(weight_class))
ufc$win_pct <- 100 * ufc$wins / ufc$total_fights
nrow(ufc)   # 2,803 athletes

# put the two defense rates on a 0-100 percent scale so coefficients are per percentage point
ufc$sig_str_defense <- 100 * ufc$sig_str_defense
ufc$takedown_defense <- 100 * ufc$takedown_defense

# keep only the variables we model, and only athletes with no missing values
model_vars <- c("win_pct", "weight_class", "age", "height", "reach", "sig_str_landed",
                "sig_str_absorbed", "sig_str_defense", "takedown_avg", "takedown_defense",
                "submission_avg", "knockdown_avg", "total_fights")
ufc <- na.omit(ufc[, model_vars])
nrow(ufc)   # 1,789 athletes

# NEW: win percentages based on only 1-4 bouts are very noisy (e.g. 1-0 = 100%), so drop them
ufc <- subset(ufc, total_fights >= 5)
nrow(ufc)   # 1,746 athletes

# NEW: group the 12 weight classes into 4 division groups so each group has enough athletes
# to estimate its own slopes (Women's Featherweight alone only had a handful of athletes)
ufc$division <- "Men Heavier"
ufc$division[ufc$weight_class %in% c("Flyweight", "Bantamweight", "Featherweight")] <- "Men Lighter"
ufc$division[ufc$weight_class %in% c("Lightweight", "Welterweight", "Middleweight")] <- "Men Middle"
ufc$division[grepl("Women", ufc$weight_class)] <- "Women"
ufc$division <- factor(ufc$division, levels = c("Men Middle", "Men Lighter", "Men Heavier", "Women"))
table(ufc$division)
```

## Training and test split

75% of athletes go in the training set and 25% go in the test set. The test set is not
touched again until the very end.

The training set is then split in half again. Following Lab 8, one half is only used to pick
the variables (stepwise selection) and the other half is only used for inference (tests,
confidence intervals, and diagnostics), so the same data is never used for both.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
train.rows <- sample(1:nrow(ufc), size = round(0.75 * nrow(ufc)))
train <- ufc[train.rows, ]
test <- ufc[-train.rows, ]

select.rows <- sample(1:nrow(train), size = round(0.5 * nrow(train)))
select.data <- train[select.rows, ]    # used for variable selection
infer.data <- train[-select.rows, ]    # used for inference and diagnostics

c(train = nrow(train), test = nrow(test), selection = nrow(select.data), inference = nrow(infer.data))
```

## Exploratory data analysis (training set only)

```{r}
# distribution of the response
summary(train$win_pct)
sd(train$win_pct)
hist(train$win_pct, breaks = 30, main = "Career Win Percentage (Training Set)",
     xlab = "Career win percentage")

# average win percentage by division group
round(tapply(train$win_pct, train$division, mean), 1)

# correlation of each numeric predictor with win percentage
num_vars <- c("age", "height", "reach", "sig_str_landed", "sig_str_absorbed", "sig_str_defense",
              "takedown_avg", "takedown_defense", "submission_avg", "knockdown_avg", "total_fights")
round(sort(cor(train[, num_vars], train$win_pct)[, 1]), 3)

# height and reach are strongly related, so check for multicollinearity
cor(train$height, train$reach)
```

Win percentage by age looked curved (it drops quickly for younger athletes and then levels
off), so we checked a quadratic term for age.

```{r}
# average win percentage in age bands
round(tapply(train$win_pct, cut(train$age, c(19, 27, 31, 35, 39, 45, 60)), mean), 1)

# compare a straight-line fit to a quadratic fit for age
age.linear <- lm(win_pct ~ age, data = train)
age.quad <- lm(win_pct ~ age + I(age^2), data = train)
summary(age.quad)$coefficients
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Career win percentage by age in the training set, with the fitted quadratic curve."
fig1 <- ggplot(train, aes(x = age, y = win_pct)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x + I(x^2), se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Age (Years)", y = "Career Win Percentage") +
  theme_bw()
fig1
ggsave("figure1_age.pdf", fig1, width = 6, height = 4)   # saved for the paper
```

```{r}
# variance inflation factors (VIF = 1 / (1 - R^2) from regressing each predictor on the others)
vif <- c()
for (v in num_vars) {
  other <- setdiff(num_vars, v)
  r2 <- summary(lm(as.formula(paste(v, "~", paste(other, collapse = " + "))), data = select.data))$r.squared
  vif[v] <- 1 / (1 - r2)
}
round(vif, 2)   # none above 10, so all predictors stay in as candidates
```

## Model fitting and variable selection (selection half)

The full model has every candidate predictor. Age (with its quadratic term) and total bouts
are included as controls. Because our research question asks whether attributes matter
equally across weight classes, every physical attribute and fighting tendency is also
allowed to interact with division group.

```{r}
full.model <- lm(win_pct ~ age + I(age^2) + total_fights +
                   (height + reach + sig_str_landed + sig_str_absorbed + sig_str_defense +
                      takedown_avg + takedown_defense + submission_avg + knockdown_avg) * division,
                 data = select.data)
length(coef(full.model))   # number of estimated parameters
AIC(full.model)

# backward stepwise selection based on AIC
step.model <- stepAIC(full.model, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
formula(step.model)
AIC(step.model)
```

## Testing the weight-class interactions (inference half)

Stepwise selection kept three interactions with division group. We test whether they are
needed using a nested F-test on the inference half, which was not used for selection.

```{r}
# selected model (with the interactions) refit on the inference half
selected.model <- lm(formula(step.model), data = infer.data)

# same model without the interaction terms
main.model <- lm(win_pct ~ age + I(age^2) + total_fights + reach + sig_str_landed +
                   sig_str_absorbed + takedown_avg + takedown_defense + submission_avg +
                   knockdown_avg + division, data = infer.data)

# nested F-test: H0 = all interaction slopes are 0
anova(main.model, selected.model)
```

The interactions were not significant, so the final model is the main-effects model.

## Final model (inference half)

```{r}
final.model <- main.model
summary(final.model)
confint(final.model)

# age where the fitted quadratic bottoms out
-coef(final.model)["age"] / (2 * coef(final.model)["I(age^2)"])
```

```{r}
# table of estimates with readable names
est <- summary(final.model)$coefficients
nice_names <- c("Intercept", "Age (years)", "Age squared", "Total professional bouts",
                "Reach (inches)", "Significant strikes landed per minute",
                "Significant strikes absorbed per minute", "Takedowns landed per 15 minutes",
                "Takedown defense (%)", "Submission attempts per 15 minutes",
                "Knockdowns landed per 15 minutes", "Division: men's lighter",
                "Division: men's heavier", "Division: women's")
results.table <- data.frame(Term = nice_names,
                            Estimate = round(est[, 1], 3),
                            SE = round(est[, 2], 3),
                            t = round(est[, 3], 2),
                            p = ifelse(est[, 4] < 0.001, "< 0.001", round(est[, 4], 3)))
kable(results.table, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Term", "Estimate", "Std. Error", "t value", "p-value"),
      caption = "Table 1. Final model fit on the inference half of the training set.")
```

## Model diagnostics (inference half)

```{r}
# residuals vs fitted values: look for patterns or changing spread
plot(final.model$fitted.values, final.model$residuals,
     xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0)

# normality of residuals: histogram, normal Q-Q plot, and Shapiro-Wilk test
hist(final.model$residuals, breaks = 30, main = "Residuals", xlab = "Residual")
qqnorm(final.model$residuals)
qqline(final.model$residuals)
shapiro.test(final.model$residuals)

# outliers: standardized residuals beyond +/- 3
std.res <- rstandard(final.model)
sum(abs(std.res) > 3)

# influential points: Cook's distance vs the 50th percentile of F(k+1, n-(k+1))
cooks <- cooks.distance(final.model)
k <- length(coef(final.model)) - 1
n <- nrow(infer.data)
cutoff <- qf(0.5, k + 1, n - (k + 1))
c(max_cooks = max(cooks), cutoff = cutoff, number_influential = sum(cooks > cutoff))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 2. Residuals versus fitted values for the final model (inference half of the training set)."
diag.data <- data.frame(fitted = final.model$fitted.values, resid = final.model$residuals)
fig2 <- ggplot(diag.data, aes(x = fitted, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Fitted Career Win Percentage", y = "Residual") +
  theme_bw()
fig2
ggsave("figure2_residuals.pdf", fig2, width = 6, height = 4)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 3. Normal Q-Q plot of the final model's residuals."
fig3 <- ggplot(diag.data, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles") +
  theme_bw()
fig3
ggsave("figure3_qq.pdf", fig3, width = 6, height = 4)
```

## Predictive performance (test set)

This is the only time the test set is used.

```{r}
test.pred <- predict(final.model, newdata = test)

# root mean squared error on the test set
test.rmse <- sqrt(mean((test$win_pct - test.pred)^2))

# R^2 on the test set: 1 - SSE / SST
test.r2 <- 1 - sum((test$win_pct - test.pred)^2) / sum((test$win_pct - mean(test$win_pct))^2)

# baseline: predict every test athlete with the training-set average
baseline.rmse <- sqrt(mean((test$win_pct - mean(train$win_pct))^2))

# RMSE on the data the model was fit to, for comparison
infer.rmse <- sqrt(mean(final.model$residuals^2))

round(c(test_rmse = test.rmse, test_r2 = test.r2, baseline_rmse = baseline.rmse,
        inference_rmse = infer.rmse), 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 4. Predicted versus actual career win percentage for athletes in the test set. The dashed line marks perfect prediction."
pred.data <- data.frame(actual = test$win_pct, predicted = test.pred)
fig4 <- ggplot(pred.data, aes(x = actual, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Actual Career Win Percentage", y = "Predicted Career Win Percentage") +
  theme_bw()
fig4
ggsave("figure4_test_predictions.pdf", fig4, width = 6, height = 4)
```
